GLM 5.3 Flash works with opencode.

Time ~14:40. 20 min to opening.

Let me write the build prompt now. Detailed spec.

Then at 15:00: create GitHub repo, push starter commit, start record, run opencode with prompt (wrapped), then screenshots, main.ts run, commit, check, submit.

Let me write prompt file now.

Prompt content:

---
You are building an entry for make.fun bounty gta6-01 ("Make GTA 6").

Work ONLY inside the current directory (/workspace/project/mf/bot). It is a git repo laid out as an entrant's repository: main.ts, serve.ts, vendor/makefun-game.ts (do not modify), game/ (the game, static files), screenshots/, shots.json, LICENSE, .makefun/owner.json.

Goal: replace the starter's simple game in game/ with the most complete, highest-quality ORIGINAL open-world crime game you can build, in the spirit of a modern open-world crime game. Original IP only: your own city name, characters, vehicles, story, art, sound. No names/logos/characters/map/music/assets from any commercial game.

MUST fulfil (all of them, visible in screenshots):
1. A 3D open city you can explore on foot and by car (streets, blocks, buildings, sidewalks, a park, a waterfront).
2. Traffic: cars driving on roads, following lanes, stopping at lights.
3. Pedestrians walking on sidewalks.
4. Vehicles you can steal and drive (enter/exit, driving physics, camera follow).
5. Wanted level (0-5 stars) that rises when you commit crimes (hitting cars/peds, shooting) and police who respond: police cars that chase you, officers that shoot.
6. Missions and a short story: at least 4 missions with objectives, dialogue text, rewards (money), progress saved.
7. Combat: on-foot shooting with a pistol, aiming, health, damage, death/respawn in hospital.
8. HUD: health bar, wanted stars, money, clock, mission objective text, minimap (canvas-drawn map with player arrow, roads, police blips, mission markers).
9. Start screen (title + Play), pause menu, and save/load (localStorage: money, missions done, position).
10. Polish: camera that feels right, effects (muzzle flash, tire smoke, screen shake), simple synthesized sound via WebAudio (engine, gunshot, siren), menus.

Tech constraints (hard):
- game/ is served as static files at a static server's root; game/index.html must open in desktop Chrome and play offline: NO network requests. Every script/image/sound/font is a file under game/ or a data: URI.
- Any library must be vendored under game/vendor/ and as a minified build named *.min.js or *.min.mjs. Use three.js: download the ESM minified build to game/vendor/three.module.min.js and map it in index.html with an import map ({"imports":{"three":"./vendor/three.module.min.js"}}).
- Limits: at most 993 files+dirs in game/, 48 MiB total, game/index.html at most 1 MiB. Every reference in index.html and in reachable .js/.mjs must resolve to a file inside game/ or a data: URI (no http(s), no protocol-relative, no CDN).
- Split the game's own source into small ES modules under game/src/ with one clear job each, named for what they do (city.js, roads.js, traffic.js, pedestrians.js, player.js, vehicles.js, police.js, wanted.js, missions.js, combat.js, hud.js, minimap.js, audio.js, save.js, ui.js, main.js). The judge reads only file names and first declarations, so naming matters.
- Keyboard + mouse controls: WASD move, mouse look, Shift sprint, E enter/exit vehicle, mouse click shoot, Tab or M map, Esc pause.

Screenshots (required, 4):
- Implement deterministic screenshot scenes: game/index.html?shot=<name>&seed=1 with names: street, car, chase, mission. Each must set up a real playable frame: street = on foot on a busy street with traffic, peds and minimap; car = driving a stolen car with traffic; chase = 3-star wanted level with police cars chasing, bullets, minimap; mission = mission objective active with marker and HUD text. Advance the simulation deterministically so the frame looks alive (traffic moving, cops positioned near player).
- Write scripts/shoot.mjs (Node, no deps beyond sharp at /workspace/project/mf/tools/node_modules/sharp) that, for each of the 4 scenes: runs chromium headless screenshot 1280x720, then converts to JPEG quality 82 into screenshots/1-street.jpg, 2-car.jpg, 3-chase.jpg, 4-mission.jpg. Command: chromium --headless=new --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --window-size=1280,720 --virtual-time-budget=6000 --screenshot=/tmp/<name>.png "file:///workspace/project/mf/bot/game/index.html?shot=<name>&seed=1". Then sharp resize 1280x720, jpeg q82 → screenshots/<n>-<name>.jpg. Delete the starter screenshots first. Keep each JPEG ≤ 250 KB, 1280x720 exactly.
- Delete starter game files you replace (game/src/*.js from the starter) so the tree is clean; keep game/index.html path.

main.ts: edit it (at least a few lines you write) — e.g., after building the dossier, log a short summary line with file counts and the entry title. Do not break it: `MAKEFUN_OUTPUT_DIR=out node main.ts` must succeed and write out/game, out/screenshots, out/dossier.json.

README.md at repo root: write it with these badges exactly (owner=sinajaa, repo=gta6-bot):
... template ...

Verification before you finish:
1. `cd /workspace/project/mf/bot && rm -rf out && mkdir -p out && MAKEFUN_OUTPUT_DIR=out node main.ts` → exit 0, dossier.json written.
2. `node scripts/shoot.mjs` → 4 JPEGs, each ≤250KB, exactly 1280x720.
3. Open each scene headlessly and confirm no console errors: chromium --headless=new --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --virtual-time-budget=4000 --dump-dom "file:///workspace/project/mf/bot/game/index.html?shot=street&seed=1" | grep -qi "<canvas" (and check the page has no external network references: grep -r "https://" game --include=*.html --include=*.js | grep -v vendor).
4. `grep -R "http" game/index.html game/src || true` must show nothing outside vendor.

Work in small steps, test in the browser via chromium headless as you go, and keep the game playable at all times. Report at the end: what you built, file list, and any known gaps.
---

That's long; opencode run takes a prompt string. Fine.

Let me write it to a file, then at 15:00 proceed.

Also note: three.js download requires network by agent — allowed (it's vendored). The agent can curl https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.min.js. But if the sandbox blocks network... opencode runs on our machine with network. OK.
